findings.failing_input: parseDate numeric branch: `new Date(Math.round((s - 25569) * 86400 * 1000))`. This is the Excel serial-date conversion (Apps Script Sheets numeric dates). For values <= 25569 (pre-1970), the conversion produces negative ms. For very large values, overflow. Not validated; downstream NaN is caught at line 143-146 but only for `Number.isNaN(d.getTime())`. Date constructor doesn't throw on extreme numbers — returns Invalid Date which getTime()→NaN. Handled.

defaultRange: `fromEpochMs = toEpochMs - DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS * 86400 * 1000` uses fixed 86400 seconds/day. If DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS spans a DST transition in some future timezone, this could shift by an hour. Currently TZ-anchored via Asia/Jerusalem formatter on both ends, and 90 days is large enough that a 1-hour drift doesn't change the calendar day. Acceptable.
findings.regression_test_idea: Spy on Date to set 'today' at IL spring-forward boundary; assert from-day calculated correctly.

findings.failing_input: defaultRange uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA')` on every call. For high-frequency calls this is slow (~100μs per format vs 10μs for cached). Only used in default-range path, not hot path.

enumerateDateRange loop `for (let t = start; t <= end; t += 86400000)` uses 24*3600*1000 in UTC. Since start/end are already UTC-anchored via Date.UTC, this is correct and DST-immune (UTC has no DST).
